newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian call money steady in modest trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian call money steady in modest trade.

text.p: Croatian interbank call money was steady at 10 percent on Thursday amid very low demand and short supply of kuna funds, money market dealers said.
One savings bank paid a higher price of 11 percent because of a perceived repayment risk.
Dealers put fresh settlements at only 9.0 million kuna by mid-morning, all of them call money.
But the central bank expected banks to increase their Lombard borrowing by the end of the day from the current 41 million kuna.
This would be necessary to tide them over until Friday, when the central bank will pay them kuna for Wednesday's sale of German marks.
Bank balances rose to 428 million kuna on Thursday from 390 million a day earlier, after they lent each other a total of 82.5 million kuna in direct off-market trade to square their positions.
This still left a shortfall of three million kuna at two banks and three other banks borrowed 50 million to maintain their mandatory reserves. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
